extractedText:
AI Film - 2 Day Workload Plan
Built for fast reference. Realistic plan = minimum good outcome. Optimistic plan = best case without losing
control.
Day 1 - Today
Goal: get all missing keyframes ready. Best case: start animating immediately after the keyframes are locked.
Realistic version
Optimistic version
Session 1 (2h)
Lock the shot list and stop branching.
Finish the missing must-have keyframes only:
27, 28-2, 29-2, 30-2, 31-2, 33, 34, 37, 39.
Do not chase polish. Readability first.
Session 1 (2h)
Lock the shot list fast and finish all missing key
story beats plus supporting frames.
Push through the full new timeline after 26 and
leave notes for motion right away.
Session 2 (2h)
Finish the remaining supporting keyframes:
12, 15, 21, 24, 25, 26, 32, 35, 38.
If a frame is fighting you, simplify composition
instead of re-solving the scene.
Session 2 (2h)
Complete all remaining keyframes and begin
first-pass animation on the strongest shots:
28-2, 30-2, 31-2, 33, 37.
Session 3 (2h)
Review all keyframes in order.
Fix only continuity breakers and weak story beats.
Export / organize everything so tomorrow starts
with zero confusion.
Session 3 (2h)
Review keyframes in order, patch the weak ones,
and animate as many core shots as possible.
Target: tomorrow begins with keyframes fully
done and several anchor shots already moving.
Today - non-negotiables
 Decide once: the alternative branch after shot 26 is the main timeline.
 Protect the key beats, not perfect mechanics.
 End the day with an ordered folder and a clear list of what is ready, weak, or missing.
Today - success test
By the end of today, you should be able to look at the keyframes in sequence and understand the film without
having to explain it to yourself.


Day 2 - Tomorrow
Goal: animate and cut the first half. Best case: finish all shots in 6 hours, then build a full rough cut in 2 hours.
Realistic version
Optimistic version
Session 1 (3h)
Animate the strongest early-half anchor shots
first.
Prioritize clarity over complexity.
Target: first half is mostly animated in rough form.
Session 1 (3h)
Move fast through all remaining shot animation,
starting with anchor beats and then filling in
supporting shots.
Do not overwork transitions.
Session 2 (3h)
Finish the first half animation and assemble the
cut for that half immediately.
Patch only obvious weak links.
Session 2 (3h)
Finish animation for the entire film in rough form.
Make every shot usable, not perfect.
Session 3 (2h)
Build a rough cut for the first half and, if time
remains, begin laying in the second half or
selecting placeholders.
Session 3 (2h)
Build the full rough cut from start to finish.
Use the edit to solve rhythm and meaning rather
than reopening shot generation.
Tomorrow - working rule
 Do not return to image generation unless a shot truly breaks the sequence.
 If the cut reads, move forward.
 Use sound, pacing, and juxtaposition to carry what the models could not show literally.
Tomorrow - success test
Realistic win: the first half is animated and cut into a readable sequence. Optimistic win: the whole film exists as
a rough cut.
When overwhelmed
 Readable beats beat perfect shots.
 A coherent sequence beats isolated beautiful fragments.
 Finished film beats unfinished ambition.
